updates.title: Google adds Gemini Decisions API for multimodal routing and checks
updates.whatChanged: Google introduced Gemini Decision 1 and the Gemini Decisions API on 11 November through the Gemini API. Gemini Decision 1 scores up to 1,000 yes/no, multiple-choice and rubric questions against shared text, image, audio, video or PDF input, and returns probabilities and confidence without output tokens. The quickstart uses API v1beta. Google lists $0.10 per million input tokens.
updates.whyCare: You can replace separate classifier calls or generated-text parsing for bounded choices, and route low-confidence results to review. IBM Granite-Switch already offers a decision adapter, so test both against your own data before changing a control path.
updates.before: Teams used generated text and parsing, standalone classifiers or hand-written rules for bounded decisions.
updates.after: Teams can score many typed questions against one multimodal input and receive option probabilities and confidence from one request.
updates.learn: Compare Gemini Decision 1 with rules, existing classifiers and Granite-Switch on labeled examples. Measure calibration, latency, cost and human-review rates. Keep deterministic policy checks for decisions that need fixed outcomes.

updates.architectureImplication: Use a bounded-choice API for routing, policy checks and context grading, then send low-confidence results to a fallback or reviewer. Keep policy enforcement outside the model.
